To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

circulating leptin levels in the pregnant ewe are related to body composition and dietary intake, and that leptin is expressed by adipose tissue and the placenta, and may have a direct role in placental and fetal growth.

circulating leptin levels in the pregnant adolescent sheep are related to maternal body composition and dietary intake and that leptin may be involved in nutrient distribution during placental and fetal growth in sheep.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of maternal nutrition on maternal and placental leptin expression and circulating leptin concentrations in relation to pregnancy outcome.
the effects of nutrition during adolescent pregnancy in sheep, with a view to improving pregnancy outcome.
understanding the role of leptin in the regulation of nutrient partitioning during pregnancy in the ovine model, and how it relates to maternal and fetal growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
leptin is not a placental hormone, but it is involved in maternal nutrition, and in fetal and placental growth.
leptin concentrations in the pregnant ewe are related to maternal body composition, and that the placenta may be a target organ for the actions of leptin.

leptin is a marker of adipose tissue mass and that it may play a role in regulating nutrient partitioning between the maternal and fetal compartments during placental growth and placental/fetal development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the circulating leptin concentration during pregnancy is a good indicator of maternal nutrition, body condition and body composition.
the circulating leptin concentrations in pregnant sheep are not a reflection of fetal or placental growth, but more a reflection of maternal body composition and dietary intake.
circulating leptin levels in the ewe are a reflection of the maternal nutritional status, with the adipose tissue being the main source of circulating leptin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the circulating leptin concentrations in the adolescent ewes reflect maternal body composition and dietary intake, and that leptin may play a role in the regulation of placental and/or foetal development.
circulating leptin levels in the ewe are a good indicator of body composition, and that the placenta appears to be a target organ for the action of leptin.
leptin is a good indicator of body fat deposition, and therefore a good predictor of body condition.
